summary: Proceed as a user-requested, below-bar run with two fixes. First, drop the T=1 target: the XL arms patch only ea4x, and decode's T=1 runs ea6 v6pe2, so it has no XL arm. Second, size is the real gate: the comment-stripped CUDA delta of patch_enc2 (~7.1 KB) is over the 6,172 B headroom unless the null X arms are dropped and the loop-trimmed consume reuses decode's consume_e.
justification: A: The mechanism holds for ea4x. L (loop-carried IMAD-stepped shared addresses, count-down, pass constants recomputed only at run ends) cuts SASS from 617 to 566 issued per record and was measured consume-only at +1.4..4.7% (T<=128) and +3..5.5% (T=256, E5XL w13 1.049-1.055, w2 1.039-1.044). All arms were bitwise to B in val+r1+r2 (research/h100-ea-enc2-1029.md). Decode's ea4x consumer loop (submission.py ~12597) has the same structure as moe's, and L's static assumptions hold there: NK=8 is a power of two (cnt0 uses b & (NK-1)), ring depth D=2, and only !DEFER twins are allowed, which matches _eae_base excluding the &256 d twins. WEAKEST LINK 1, a factual error: the `change` and the `expected` decode_1 row claim 'XL trims K1/K2 loops' at T=1. patch_enc2.py edits only ea_kernels.cuh (consume_lt) and ea4x_kernels.cuh. Decode's T=1 is the ea6 v6pe2 route (_eae_t1core / _eae_src6, EAE_T1 33/44/30), so no XL arm exists for it and T=1 cannot move. An ea6 L port would be new and not node-validated. Remove the decode_1 expectation and cut value_gain accordingly (T=256 cold half + small T=8..128 consume gains; realistic headline +0.3..0.6%). WEAKEST LINK 2: the lane's own verdict says normal mode reads 0.97-1.03 (HBM wall), and L3/L4 transferred at 0.5-0.8x. The T=256 case rests on the iso pair moving from .979 [.977,.981] / E5 .978 [.975,.983] to <= .98 in every round. A 2-4% iso cut does that, so this is plausible. It is not a port: decode's ea4x has no runtime-dq selector (`dq >= 2 && dq <= 4` is absent). Decode wires E arms by rewriting template instances (_eae_src4x maps <2,false>/<2,true> to <3>/<4> and pdl bit 4096). XL therefore needs re-authoring in decode's _eae_* string-patch style: new instances <27>/<28> (DQ&7 / DQ&16 decoding inside the template), a new dispatch bit, new _EAE_CORES keys, and per-class race entries. consume_lt must be byte-equivalent in arithmetic to decode's consume_e<DQ,0,1>, not to moe's consume_enc. The scale offsets match: DQ3 g*32 and g*32+256, DQ4 g*64+kq*16. The ext_a4b / scale_pair_imad_rt / mul_bf16x2_h call sequence must be copied from consume_e. prior: correctly names the landed stack it extends. Not on any do-not-retry line.
confounders: engine-a-encodings-wh5ds-decode-stack (landed, CLAIMS.md:101): this is the base, and its E race is the routing machine XL rides in. T=128/256 hot halves are wh5ds, so XL only touches the Engine A cold half there. A T=256 move is the cold-half pair only. The wh5ds hot half and the H-16 hybrid are unchanged, but the iso pair ratio is measured with the hot half co-running (layer-nondet), so the iso readings carry the same coupling noise that left T=256 at .979-.983.

Engine A v4x decode port / v4c cost-weighted split (CLAIMS.md:93, :55): L's run logic (cnt0 / super-group ends / ticket path) runs on v4c's runtime-chosen b/e boundaries. Moe's bench exercised its own grids, not decode's v4cxs splits, so bitwise must be re-proven on decode's partial-super-group cases at every routed T.
T=16 pinned v4cxs (CLAIMS.md:83, :101): the pin stays. XL at T=16 is only an E-code swap inside v4cxs, which is consistent.
interference: No companion. Every XL arm is raced per class against the incumbent E4/E5 and master under the existing exact + iso<=0.98 every round + layer veto<=1.00 gates, so a loss self-vetoes back to today's routes and a gain is attributed per class by the [ea-enc] printout. An ab-revert of the landed E stack would remove the machinery XL needs. A control that separates X from L is pointless because X was null on the node; drop X instead.
rules_flags: None on precision: XL is bitwise E4/E5, which is already exact against master. The build must still pass decode's exact check per class with the XL arms.

Size cap 1,000,000 B: headroom is 6,172 B. patch_enc2's CUDA replacements are +8,663 B raw and +7,092 B comment-stripped, which is OVER before any Python wiring. Required: drop E4X/E5X (dq 11/12, null on the node). Implement L by giving decode's consume_e an address-form entry, or a template flag, instead of a full consume_lt copy. Keep comments minimal in the injected strings. Trim Python only (comments/dead branches) and leave other CUDA strings byte-identical. Abort the run if the final size is >= 1,000,000.
freshness: E: CLAIMS.md:101 [landed] engine-a-encodings-wh5ds-decode-stack is the base this extends with the same mechanism (E-code race), so it is not a different owner of the rows. CLAIMS.md:100 [shelf] wh5ds hot half was absorbed into :101 and is unaffected. BEST 1.7051 (e42339989d554019), blob 4f529d7b = mint blob, moved 0.00% vs 1.24% margin: fresh. Below the value bar (and lower than stated once T=1 is removed), but user_requested under the expert-block focus, so it is allowed.
open_questions: Build must print: (1) final submission.py size in bytes vs 1,000,000; (2) [ea-enc] build line with the 4x build seconds (39 s today with 4 instances; ~2x with E4XL/E5XL w13+w2 added; it must finish before phase at ~126 s, or the join wait counts against EAE_JOIN_S 220) and regs/lmem/occ for K1/K2 e4xl/e5xl (node 92-94 regs, 0 spill; confirm occ stays 2 as for e4/e5 at 82-83); (3) the state-copy check; (4) per class T=8/16/32/128/256: iso E4, E5, E4XL, E5XL with CI and per-round max, exact (bitwise vs E4/E5 and vs master) per arm, layer s/f for the winner; (5) PATH CHOSEN per class, with T=1 shown explicitly as 'no XL arm (ea6)'; (6) prepare-at time (128 s today of the 900 s run budget).
At T=128/256 does the cold half ever produce nr>8 passes? L only trims the one-tile path (nr<=8), and nr>8 falls back to consume2 unchanged, so the gain dilutes if cold passes exceed 8 routes.
If E5XL wins T=256 iso but the T=256 layer stays 'layer-nondet' (no layer gate ran in 824b60fa), confirm which veto decides T=256 so it is not routed on iso alone.
